newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 23.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The tribunal investigating payments to politicians does not have the power to force former Prime Minister Charles Haughey, alleged recipient of 1.3 million pounds, to give evidence.

- Health minister Michael Nonnan edged closer to a settlement package with victims of a tainted blood scandal, following up an offer of 200 million pounds damages with an additional 30 million pounds.
- International fraud is costing the European Union up to 50
billion pounds a year, according to an EU sponsored
- Irish business tycoon Ben Dunne claimed that he gave former Irish Prime Minister Charles Haughey bank drafts totalling 210,000 pounds, the tribunal investigating payments to politicians was told.
- Peruvian troops dramtically ended the 126-day hostage crisis at the Japanese embassy in Lima.
- The government is to offer an addition 30 million pounds to victims of a tainted blood scandal, bringing the total to 230 million pounds.

- A former associate of businssman Ben Dunne has supported Dunne's allegation that he gave almost 1.3 million pounds to former Prime Minister Charles Haughey. This was stated by Noel Fox, an accountant and trustee of Dunnes Settlement Trust. - Peruvian troops stormed the Japanese embassy and ended a 126-day hostage drama.

- The Central Bank has intervened heavily in currency markets to hold up the value of the pound against sterling. The pound rose against the German mark on Tuesday but kept its position against sterling thanks to the intervention.
